subtopic: CUDA / Online softmax — tile-wise running max and sum
learningObjective: Understand the online softmax recurrence used to compute softmax in tiles without materializing the full row.
stem: The online-softmax recurrence processes a row of length N in tiles of size B (with T = N/B tiles). Let `(m_t, s_t)` be the running (max, sum-of-exp-with-max-subtracted) after tile t. Which update rule is correct when a new tile `x_new` (of size B) with local max `m_new` and local sum `s_new = sum(exp(x_new - m_new))` arrives?

options.text: `m` remains `m_prev` and `s = s_prev + s_new * exp(m_new)`; the running max is never updated after the first tile because subsequent tiles' contributions are absolutely negligible.
`m = m_prev + m_new` and `s = s_prev + s_new`; the recurrence is a straightforward sum-of-parts because addition is commutative and softmax is scale-invariant.

`m = max(m_prev, m_new)`; `s = s_prev * exp(m_prev - m) + s_new * exp(m_new - m)`. The old sum is rescaled by `exp(m_prev - m)` (a value in (0, 1]) to reflect the new anchor; the new tile's sum by `exp(m_new - m)`. This is exact algebra: the merged tile is anchored at the new max.
The online softmax recurrence works only for FP16 inputs because FP32 overflows before the second rescale; the algorithm is FlashAttention-specific and not applicable to plain softmax kernels.

explanation: The online-softmax recurrence, popularized by Milakov & Gimelshein and central to FlashAttention, updates a running `(m, s)` per tile such that after processing all tiles the pair equals `(max(x_1..N), sum_i exp(x_i - max))`. When a new tile arrives, the new anchor is `m = max(m_prev, m_new)`; the previously accumulated `s_prev` was anchored at `m_prev`, so it is rescaled by `exp(m_prev - m)` (≤ 1 since m ≥ m_prev). The new tile's `s_new` (anchored at `m_new`) is rescaled by `exp(m_new - m)`. This is exact algebra, not an approximation.

optionExplanations.B: Wrong: naive sum ignores anchor rescaling and gives wrong result.
optionExplanations.A: Wrong: fails when a later tile has larger max.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: FP32 works fine; algorithm is general-purpose.

assumptions: FP32 accumulation with well-behaved input ranges.
nonImplications: Does not imply the recurrence is only useful for attention; any tile-wise softmax benefits.
Does not imply the recurrence is bitwise-associative; order still matters at FP-rounding scale.

distractorRationales.A: Ignores updates to the running max.
